## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

01net (French): the PHP2Shell flaws are a headache for the whole Internet because PHP is everywhere and often invisible, so organisations struggle to find where it runs; some public sites are going offline as a precaution. Experts at the security firm Filigran say the real challenge is not fixing PHP's code but locating every deployment, and compare the situation to Log4Shell.

> PHP2Shell réunit bon nombre des ingrédients de Log4Shell : une exécution de code à distance sans authentification, dans un logiciel présent presque partout

## What the page says

_The watch reader's English summary (researcher@php.newsroom, languages pass of 22 October 2026), not the publisher's words:_

20minutos explains why European governments, hospitals and schools disconnected their sites. It cites an EU joint statement, a warning from BSI vice-president Thomas Caspers, and a detailed (EFE-sourced) list of Belgian shutdowns: the Flemish government, federal ministries, Smartschool, VRT, Antwerp hospitals and vdk bank. It also covers Germany's Charité and Spain's INCIBE critical notice.

## Verbatim quotes, with the watch reader's translation

Each quote is in the snapshot as served. The English is the source watch reader's translation (`translations/es/news/20minutos/tecnologia-ciberseguridad-por-que-gobiernos-hospitales-coleg.json`), not the publisher's and not checked word for word by the curator.

**agency**: A joint communiqué from the European Commission, ENISA, CERT-EU, Europol and the EU CSIRTs network advised considering disconnection of exposed applications that cannot be patched.

> la Comisión Europea, ENISA, CERT-EU, Europol y la red europea de equipos de respuesta aconsejan en su comunicado conjunto considerar la desconexión de las aplicaciones expuestas a internet hasta poder corregirlas.

_Watch reader's translation:_ the European Commission, ENISA, CERT-EU, Europol and the European network of response teams advise in their joint communiqué considering disconnecting internet-exposed applications until they can be fixed.

**official**: BSI vice-president Thomas Caspers warned that large-scale exploitation within hours of the patch release was likely (via EFE).

> “Consideramos probable que se produzca un aprovechamiento a gran escala y a corto plazo, en las pocas horas siguientes a la publicación de las actualizaciones de seguridad”.

_Watch reader's translation:_ "We consider it likely that large-scale exploitation will occur in the short term, within the few hours following the publication of the security updates."

**offline**: The Flemish government ordered its PHP-based official websites taken down, including the regional Parliament portal; federal FPS Foreign Affairs, Finance and Employment sites also went down.

> el Gobierno flamenco ordenó retirar temporalmente sus webs oficiales que funcionan con PHP. La medida alcanzó al portal del Parlamento regional y coincidió con la desconexión de páginas de los servicios públicos federales de Asuntos Exteriores, Finanzas y Empleo.

_Watch reader's translation:_ the Flemish government ordered the temporary withdrawal of its official PHP-based websites. The measure reached the regional Parliament portal and coincided with the disconnection of pages of the federal public services for Foreign Affairs, Finance and Employment.

**offline**: School platform Smartschool and public broadcaster VRT's sites were unavailable in Belgium.

> Las familias también encontraron inaccesible Smartschool, la plataforma que utilizan los colegios para comunicarse con padres y alumnos. Varias webs de medios de comunicación, entre ellas las de la radiotelevisión pública flamenca VRT, quedaron igualmente fuera de servicio

_Watch reader's translation:_ Families also found Smartschool, the platform schools use to communicate with parents and pupils, inaccessible. Several media websites, including those of the Flemish public broadcaster VRT, were likewise out of service

**offline**: Two Antwerp hospitals (AZ Monica and university hospital UZA) took their sites down; vdk bank took its corporate site down while online banking continued.

> Dos hospitales de Amberes, AZ Monica y el universitario UZA, retiraron sus páginas. El banco vdk bank hizo lo mismo con su web corporativa, aunque aseguró que la banca electrónica continuaba funcionando.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Two Antwerp hospitals, AZ Monica and the university hospital UZA, took down their pages. The bank vdk bank did the same with its corporate website, although it said online banking continued to work.

**agency**: The Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium said it had no knowledge of actual incidents in the country at that time.

> el Centro para la Ciberseguridad de Bélgica precisó que, en ese momento, no tenía constancia de incidentes reales en el país.

_Watch reader's translation:_ the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium specified that, at that time, it had no record of actual incidents in the country.

**offline**: In the Netherlands, the Parliament and MijnOverheid went offline alongside DigiD; in Germany administrations, universities and hospitals including Charité did too.

> En Países Bajos, las desconexiones preventivas afectaron al Parlamento, al portal gubernamental MijnOverheid y a DigiD

_Watch reader's translation:_ In the Netherlands, the preventive disconnections affected Parliament, the government portal MijnOverheid and DigiD

**agency**: Spain's INCIBE issued a critical-importance notice urging updates and, if not possible, isolation of exposed systems from public networks.

> En España, el Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (Incibe) también ha emitido un aviso de importancia crítica y ha pedido instalar las actualizaciones cuanto antes.

_Watch reader's translation:_ In Spain, the National Cybersecurity Institute (Incibe) has also issued a critical-importance notice and has asked for updates to be installed as soon as possible.

- Site title "CGA". Plain curl to cyber.gov.au timed out from this egress, but Playwright got 200.

ASD's ACSC recommends organisations: - Identify PHP within their environments - Review the latest PHP guidance at https://www.php.net/index.php - Apply available security updates and other appropriate mitigations - Monitor PHP applications and related systems for suspicious activity."
- The older body text is still pre-patch: "Prepare to update and apply security patches as they become available." It also says "full details publicly announced on Thursday 22 October 2026 at 0100 AEDT" (= 2026-10-21T14:00Z). The summary line still reads "is set for public disclosure on 22 October 2026."
- "ASD’s ACSC is not aware of successful active exploitation within Australia".
- **No take-offline or isolation advice.** This contradicts the BBC framing that the Australian counterpart issued advice like the NCSC/NSA. The ACSC advice is patch, mitigate and monitor.

# Offline door PHP kwetsbaarheden: Welke Nederlandse websites waren uit de lucht?

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`), page `nl/news/agconnect/maatschappij-security-welke-nederlandse-websites-waren-uit-d`, snapshot `20261022T181608Z`. URL: https://www.agconnect.nl/maatschappij/security/welke-nederlandse-websites-waren-uit-de-lucht

## What the page says

_The watch reader's English summary (researcher@php.newsroom, languages pass of 22 October 2026), not the publisher's words:_

AG Connect lists Dutch websites that went offline: at least 13 of 25 safety regions, the Schiphol app, the Port of Rotterdam, Odido's BEN and Simpel brands, many political parties, the Tweede Kamer and MijnOverheid, several hospitals, AG Connect itself and supermarket Hoogvliet. Most central government (Rijksoverheid) sites stayed up because they do not use PHP.

## Verbatim quotes, with the watch reader's translation

Each quote is in the snapshot as served. The English is the source watch reader's translation (`translations/nl/news/agconnect/maatschappij-security-welke-nederlandse-websites-waren-uit-d.json`), not the publisher's and not checked word for word by the curator.

**number**: At least 13 of the 25 Dutch safety regions took their websites offline, including IJsselland, Twente, Gelderland-Midden, Noord-Holland-Noord, Rotterdam-Rijnmond and Zeeland.

> Zo gingen de websites van zeker dertien van de 25 veiligheidsregio's in Nederland offline.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Thus the websites of at least thirteen of the 25 safety regions in the Netherlands went offline.

**offline**: Schiphol took the Schiphol app offline as a precaution, while its website stayed up with a notice about a global digital threat.

> Schiphol haalde de Schiphol-app uit voorzorg uit de lucht.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Schiphol took the Schiphol app offline as a precaution.

**offline**: The Port of Rotterdam temporarily took its website offline, saying there were no signs of concrete security problems.

> Ook het Havenbedrijf Rotterdam heeft zijn website tijdelijk offline gehaald, maar gaf aan dat er geen signalen waren dat de situatie tot concrete veiligheidsproblemen leidde.

_Watch reader's translation:_ The Port of Rotterdam Authority also temporarily took its website offline, but indicated there were no signs that the situation led to concrete security problems.

**offline**: Telecom company Odido took the sites of its brands BEN and Simpel offline; Odido's own site does not use PHP.

> Telecombedrijf Odido heeft uit voorzorgeen de sites van de merken BEN en Simpel offline gehaald.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Telecom company Odido took the sites of the brands BEN and Simpel offline as a precaution.

**offline**: VVD, CDA, PRO, BBB and PvdD said their sites were taken offline preventively; D66, SGP, ChristenUnie, DENK and JA21 sites were also offline.

> VVD, CDA, PRO, BBB en PvdD hebben ook laten weten dat hun sites preventief offline zijn gehaald vanwege het risico.

_Watch reader's translation:_ VVD, CDA, PRO, BBB and PvdD have also announced that their sites were taken offline preventively because of the risk.

**offline**: Several hospital sites were unreachable, including Maastricht UMC+, Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis, BovenIJ, Albert Schweitzer Ziekenhuis, Haaglanden MC, St. Antonius and Elisabeth-TweeSteden.

> De sites van onder meer Maastricht UMC+, het Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis in Den Bosch, BovenIJ in Amsterdam en het Albert Schweitzer Ziekenhuis in Dordrecht waren niet bereikbaar.

_Watch reader's translation:_ The sites of, among others, Maastricht UMC+, the Jeroen Bosch Hospital in Den Bosch, BovenIJ in Amsterdam and the Albert Schweitzer Hospital in Dordrecht were not reachable.

**other**: Most Dutch central-government organisation websites kept working because they do not use PHP.

> De meeste websites van rijksoverheidsorganisaties werkten nog wel gewoon. Die maken geen gebruik van PHP.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Most websites of central government organisations still worked normally. They do not use PHP.

**offline**: Supermarket chain Hoogvliet took its website offline; AG Connect and sister titles such as iBestuur were also taken offline.

> Supermarktketen Hoogvliet haalde echter wel de website uit de lucht.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Supermarket chain Hoogvliet did, however, take its website offline.

# Amazon Threat Intelligence identifies PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure in MadPot | AWS Security Blog

Captured by claude-story-site. Status: captured. Primary account of the 17 October honeypot attempt and the 02:00 UTC proof-of-concept attempts; 'PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild'.

- By CJ Moses, 21 Oct 2026. Verbatim: 'identified a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt dating to Oct. 17, 2026, in MadPot telemetry, four days before public disclosure'; 'originated from an IP address associated with a commercial anonymization network'; 'it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure'.
- 'multiple proof of concept exploits for the vulnerability, with the earliest around 2026-10-21 0200 UTC'; attempts 02:00 to 08:00 UTC from additional anonymised infrastructure, 'multiple actors'; 'it's unclear if any of these attempts would have succeeded in real-world systems'.
- After release: 'PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild.' No counts.
- Advice: investigate from 17 October; detections that do not rely on a CVE signature; consider blocking multipart uploads where you cannot patch.
- A reader comment complains AWS managed distributions lacked packages for 10 hours (unverified).

# BBC News live page: notes

- URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/ckgel5xp2xv9t, which redirects to https://www.bbc.com/news/live/ckgel5xp2xv9t
- Live since 2026-10-22T06:16Z (seoTimestamps.firstPublished 06:16:24.321Z); edited by Kieran Kelly and Imogen James

- The 08:00 BST post appeared after 07:55Z: "No evidence that hackers have exploited flaw so far, says researcher" (Ryan Austin, Calif).

## Claims attributed here (follow each to its primary source)
- PHP Foundation: coordinated disclosure "worked well" until a leak; Calif "mistakenly published a video". Find the foundation's statement.
- OpenAI "Patch the Planet" initiative; the PHP Foundation was accepted in July 2026. Find OpenAI's blog post.
- Calif found the flaw in August; OpenAI and Wiz found it independently shortly after. Find the Calif and Wiz posts.
- Wiz: "roughly 70%" of the internet affected. The BBC could not verify this.
- Woodward: "something like 30 million websites"
- NSA cyber (X post): "two critical vulnerabilities". Take offline if an update is not feasible.
- NCSC note: "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline". Also EU and Australian counterparts.
- Amazon and Cloudflare saw probing (Woodward). Find Cloudflare's or AWS's own statement.
- Affected: Wikipedia (parts taken down), Edinburgh council, French government sites, the University of Geneva (header image), online shops, the BBC.
- In 2024 PHP Foundation researchers found a theoretical flaw they could not exploit.
- Not in the blog: CVE IDs, affected versions or SAPIs, the patched releases. Get these from php.net.

notes_md:
# Calif: "php2shell by Calif Research" — notes (collector-researchers)

- URL: https://calif.io/php2shell/ (linked from the calif.io homepage banner "Calif discovered php2shell"). Captured 2026-10-22T08:10:33Z, HTTP 200.
- Date: no machine-readable publish time; the comic timeline's last panel reads "Oct 21, 2026 and here we are...". Credits: "Research and writeup by Ryan Austin (@lcfr_hax) of Calif ... Poster and comic story by Michal Zalewski (@lcamtuf) of Calif."
- Framing: "two PHP remote vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) discovered by Calif, OpenAI and Wiz".

## Calif's timeline (verbatim from "An interesting timeline of events")
- "2026 — August 1 Calif discovered multiple different paths independently leading to RCE that resurfaced the 2024 issues and new trigger points."
- "2026 — August 5 Calif researcher Ryan Austin (@lcfr_hax) tweeted hash of one finding." (links https://x.com/lcfr_hax/status/2085031675382071483)
- "2026 — August 11 Calif reported the first bug to PHP and started coordinated disclosure process."
- "2026 — August 14 Calif shared an RCE PoC with PHP."
- "2026 — August 15 PHP confirmed that the RCE PoC worked as expected."
- "2026 — August 21 Calif reported the second bug to PHP."
- "2026 — October 21 Patched versions released."
- Comic panel 4: "July 30, 2026 Patch the Planet ... OpenAI invited us to join its Patch the Planet initiative ... Stefan connected us with Volker Dusch, who accepted our invitation."
- 2024 panel: "OSTIF and Quarkslab performed an audit of PHP and rediscovered the same OOM issue. However, exploitation was not proven, hence the bug was not fixed."

## AI angle
- "No special harness, or access to models that weren't generally available to everyone were used in the initial bug discovery." Austin: "I asked my LLM companion for help." Model is NOT named on this page (press says GPT-5.6 Sol).
- "We were not expecting to find anything critical - everyone and every lab had already done extensive AI assisted audits of this target."

## Exploit demos (not downloaded)
- Page embeds "Here is a demo video of the exploits running:" YouTube iframes: youtube-nocookie.com/embed/pfWZrdzvooc ("php2shell exploit demonstration") and /embed/cE4h79AWbT4 ("Exploiting Nginx with PHP-FPM"). Claims confirmed pre-auth RCE on WordPress 7.1.2, Drupal 11.4.3, Joomla 6.1.4, MediaWiki, Roundcube, Magento, phpMyAdmin, Nextcloud, Laravel, Symfony, WHMCS.
- Whether pfWZrdzvooc is the same video the PHP Foundation says Calif "mistakenly published" on Oct 20 is UNKNOWN. The page does not mention the leak or the deleted video at all.

## Contradictions
- Calif: discovery Aug 1; first report Aug 11. Fortune repeats Aug 1. PHP Foundation: Calif's audit began July 30, report Aug 11 (agrees).
- Calif homepage also links two archive.is snapshots (arHsF, spwCf), probably of WSJ/NYT coverage — not checked.

**offline**: Federal court TRF1 suspended external access to SEI, following a recommendation from TRF4; no restoration time given.

**offline**: The federal courts of the 4th Region (Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Paraná) cut external access to their systems from 11:00 on Wednesday.

> O Centro de Prevenção, Tratamento e Resposta a Incidentes Cibernéticos de Governo (CTIR Gov), ligado ao Gabinete de Segurança Institucional da Presidência, também publicou um alerta oficial nesta quarta-feira (21).

title: Security Advisory 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
notes: v1.0 and v1.1 both 21/10/2026. States the PHP fixes were released '21 October 2026 at 13:30 UTC'. CVSS 9.2 each. Advice: 'patch affected assets immediately. Where that is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is applied and verified.' Notes PoCs are circulating.
notes_md:
# CERT-EU Security Advisory 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP

- Stated "Release Date: 21-10-2026 15:20:18" (no timezone; CERT-EU is in Brussels, so probably CEST = 13:20Z, but that is not stated). History: v1.0 "Initial publication" and v1.1 "Updates with additional information", both 21/10/2026.
- Captured 2026-10-22T08:13:29Z.
- Key claims (verbatim):
  - "On 20 October 2026, the PHP project announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities in PHP"
  - "The PHP team released the fixes today, 21 October 2026 at 13:30 UTC, in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35"
  - "Technical details are now being discussed publicly, and initial proofs of concept (PoCs) have begun to circulate. This raises the likelihood that attackers are already exploiting the vulnerabilities."
  - CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w), CVSS 9.2, OOM memory corruption; CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp), CVSS 9.2, stale global state.
  - "The PHP team considers mod_php the highest-risk setup."
- Exact advice: "CERT-EU advises organisations to patch affected assets immediately. Where that is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is applied and verified." Repeated under Recommendations as "isolating internet-facing resources from public networks".
- Temporary mitigations: memory_limit=-1 set via php_admin_value; low post_max_size; proxy-level request limits; cgroup memory limit (not RLIMIT_AS); session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restart workers; on 8.5 fatal_error_backtraces=0.
- Notes "rpms.remirepo.net ... will not have updates on release day".
- Its references include a Mastodon post by @GossiTheDog (cyberplace.social/@GossiTheDog/117474220875882526) and an X post by watchTowr (x.com/watchtowrcyber/status/2112611507749982605) as "public reports". Those are for the social/researcher collectors.
- Differs from CERT-FR on the release time: CERT-FR quotes PHP's pre-announcement of 16:00 Paris (14:00 UTC); CERT-EU says released 13:30 UTC.

title: [Màj] Multiples vulnérabilités dans PHP (CERTFR-2026-ALE-014)
notes: First and last version 21 Oct 2026. 'Le CERT-FR recommande d'isoler les équipements affectés puis de procéder à la migration vers une version maintenue...'. Affected: all 5.x, 6.x, 7.x, 8.0, 8.1, and 8.2-8.5 below the fixed versions. Workarounds: session.upload_progress off; block multipart Content-Type at WAF.
notes_md:
# CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-014: [Màj] Multiples vulnérabilités dans PHP

- New domain: cert.cyber.gouv.fr (the old www.cert.ssi.gouv.fr redirects with a 302).
- "Date de la première version 21 octobre 2026"; "Date de la dernière version 21 octobre 2026". Two versions: the initial one, then "Mises à jour des risques, des systèmes affectés et ajout des correctifs de sécurité".
- Captured 2026-10-22T08:13:53Z.
- Key lines (verbatim, French):
  - "L'éditeur annonce la disponibilité des correctifs de sécurité pour le 21 octobre 2026 à 16h00 heure de Paris (14h00 UTC)." (This is PHP's pre-announced time; CERT-EU says the fixes came out at 13:30 UTC.)
  - Advice: "Le CERT-FR recommande d'isoler les équipements affectés puis de procéder à la migration vers une version maintenue et avec les derniers correctifs de sécurité dès publication du correctif éditeur." In English: CERT-FR recommends isolating affected equipment, then migrating to a maintained, patched version once the vendor fix is out.
  - Workarounds "non qualifiés par le CERT-FR": session.upload_progress.enabled = Off (plus php_admin_flag for FPM); "bloquer toutes requêtes HTTP dont l'en-tête contient un Content-Type positionné à la valeur multipart", or failing that, monitor such requests; can be done at a WAF.
- Affected: "PHP toutes versions 5.x, 6.x, 7.x, 8.0.x, 8.1.x" plus 8.2 to 8.5 below the fixed versions.
- Also references CERTFR-2026-AVI-1359 and the reflex sheet CERTFR-2025-RFX-002 (edge-device compromise containment).
- Of all the agencies, CERT-FR's advice is the closest to "isolate first": isolate, THEN migrate.

notes_md:
# CERT.LV: Latvia introduces preventive measures over the PHP vulnerabilities

- Page date 2026-10-21. "[Informācija publicēta 21.10.2026, plkst. 18:25]" = published 18:25 local (EEST, UTC+3), so 15:25Z. "[Informācija papildināta: 21.10.2026, plkst. 23:00]" = updated 23:00 local, so 20:00Z. The UTC conversion is ours.
- Captured 2026-10-22T08:13:54Z. The text is Latvian; the translations below are ours, so check them before publishing.
- Original post (18:25): to protect state information systems, "pieņemts lēmums uz laiku ierobežot piekļuvi vairākiem valsts digitālajiem resursiem no ārvalstīm". A decision was made to temporarily restrict access to several state digital resources FROM ABROAD. Applied selectively. "Piekļuves ierobežojumi varētu būt spēkā līdz pirmdienai, 26. oktobrim". The restrictions may last until Monday 26 October. Residents in Latvia should not be affected. No known compromise in Latvia.
- Advice: update to 8.5.12/8.4.27/8.3.36/8.2.35. "Sistēmām, kuras nav iespējams atjaunināt uz drošu PHP versiju, ir jāierobežo piekļuve no interneta, nepieļaujot to publisku pieejamību līdz drošības risku novēršanai." Systems that cannot be updated MUST have internet access restricted, with no public availability until the risk is removed.
- Update (23:00): the unified website platform (TVP) for state and municipal sites is patched and reachable again from Latvia. Latvija.gov.lv is reachable from Latvia and restricted only from abroad. lsm.lv (public broadcaster) and 112.lv have been restored. Other state resources keep their foreign-access restrictions. "Kopumā Latvijā identificēti aptuveni 6000 potenciāli ietekmētu resursu, no kuriem tikai daži simti ir valsts sektorā." Around 6,000 potentially affected resources in Latvia, a few hundred of them in the state sector. "Latvijā jau ir konstatēti automatizēti mēģinājumi izmantot PHP ievainojamības, taču līdz šim nav ziņu par sekmīgiem uzbrukumiem." Automated exploitation attempts have been seen in Latvia; no successful attacks reported so far.
- This is a concrete case of government services being taken off the public internet: geo-blocked, not fully down. lsm.lv and 112.lv were evidently restricted too (they were "restored").

The rest is CISA's standard text on Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04, which applies only to Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies, and its encouragement to all organisations to prioritise KEV vulnerabilities.

The due date (2026-10-29) and the ransomware field ("Unknown") are in the catalog itself, captured at the same pass as `cisa-kev-json` and `cisa-kev-catalog` (catalog version 2026.10.26, released 2026-10-26T22:24:24Z). # CISA Alert: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching

- URL: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/21/critical-vulnerabilities-php-require-immediate-patching. "Release Date October 21, 2026" (no time given).
- Captured 2026-10-22T08:13:53Z with Playwright. Plain curl to www.cisa.gov returns 403 (Akamai), but the headless browser gets 200. The CISA home page (`cisa-home`) lists it at the top as "OCT 21, 2026 ALERT".

  - "CISA strongly urges organizations to immediately patch the recently disclosed critical vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619."
  - "Organizations should immediately update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35"
  - "Identify and inventory systems running any version of PHP across your organization."
  - "Apply the patch immediately, prioritizing internet-facing systems."
  - "Organizations that cannot update immediately, or that continue to use PHP 8.1 or earlier unsupported versions, should take PHP-based systems offline until they can be patched or updated."
  - "A web application firewall may provide some protection until systems are updated or patched."
  - "Monitor for suspicious activity, including PHP worker processes launching shells or downloading tools."

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`), page `br/news/cointelegraph/news-php-foundation-admits-structural-failure-delayed-critic`, snapshot `20261022T181608Z`. ## What the page says

_The watch reader's English summary (researcher@php.newsroom, languages pass of 22 October 2026), not the publisher's words:_

Cointelegraph Brasil covers the PHP Foundation's admission that a 'structural failure' delayed the fix, and the worldwide shutdowns. It adds Australia's ASD, Japan's prime minister, crypto-sector exposure data from SlowMist, and Cardano's Intersect taking its member area offline.

## Verbatim quotes, with the watch reader's translation

Each quote is in the snapshot as served. The English is the source watch reader's translation (`translations/br/news/cointelegraph/news-php-foundation-admits-structural-failure-delayed-critic.json`), not the publisher's and not checked word for word by the curator.

**offline**: France's Interior Ministry temporarily took prefecture websites offline, and Germany's federal IT provider ITZBund disabled several sites (attributed to Reuters).

> o Ministério do Interior da França temporariamente tirou do ar os sites das prefeituras. A provedora federal de TI da Alemanha, ITZBund, também desativou vários sites, segundo a Reuters.

_Watch reader's translation:_ France's Interior Ministry temporarily took the prefecture websites offline. Germany's federal IT provider, ITZBund, also disabled several sites, according to Reuters.

**offline**: Australia's Signals Directorate acknowledged that its cyber.gov.au site was among the government sites affected.

> Na Austrália, a Diretoria de Sinais Australiana reconheceu que seu site de cibersegurança, cyber.gov.au, estava entre os sites governamentais afetados pelo problema do PHP.

_Watch reader's translation:_ In Australia, the Australian Signals Directorate acknowledged that its cybersecurity website, cyber.gov.au, was among the government sites affected by the PHP problem.

**official**: Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi posted on X urging site operators to patch quickly and suggesting temporary suspension if they could not.

> A primeira-ministra do Japão, Sanae Takaichi, publicou no X um apelo para que os operadores de sites se preparassem para aplicar o patch o mais rápido possível.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Japan's Prime Minister, Sanae Takaichi, posted on X an appeal for site operators to prepare to apply the patch as quickly as possible.

**number**: SlowMist's MistEye found 793 domains with direct PHP fingerprints among 1,488 crypto-sector domains assessed.

> Foram identificados 793 domínios com impressões digitais diretas de PHP entre os 1.488 domínios avaliados.

_Watch reader's translation:_ 793 domains with direct PHP fingerprints were identified among the 1,488 domains assessed.

**offline**: Intersect, the Cardano governance member organisation, took its Member Area offline while assessing exposure; it was still down at time of writing.

> A Intersect, uma organização associativa que apoia o desenvolvimento e a governança da blockchain Cardano, afirmou que havia temporariamente tirado do ar sua Área de Membros enquanto avaliava uma possível exposição.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Intersect, a membership organisation supporting Cardano blockchain development and governance, said it had temporarily taken its Members Area offline while assessing possible exposure.

_Curator's reading of the capture._

ConvergenciaDigital (Brazil, Portuguese), 26 October, by Ana Paula Lobo, relaying GlobalData's social-media analyst Smitarani Tripathy: influencers on X have been discussing PHP2Shell since 21 October as proof that cyber-security is entering a phase where speed matters as much as severity, with exploitation attempts appearing within hours of disclosure after the flaws, present for over a decade, were demonstrated through AI-assisted research. > Segundo o analista, os influenciadores preveem que o PHP2Shell seja um modelo, e não uma exceção, com mais vulnerabilidades críticas por vir

notes: CVE record JSON in raw/ (cveawg API). dateReserved 2026-10-12T21:03:58Z, datePublished 2026-10-21T13:48:34Z, dateUpdated 2026-10-21T16:07:52Z at fetch. CISA ADP SSVC at 14:34Z: Exploitation none, Automatable no, Technical Impact total.
notes_md:
# CVE-2026-109618 (cve.org record): notes
- Page captured 08:12Z; raw/cveawg-api.json is the full CVE JSON 5.2 record, fetched 08:11Z.
- CNA: PHP Group (assignerShortName "php"). Title "RCE via OOM corruption".
- Description (verbatim): "PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE)."
- Affected: 8.2.* lessThan 8.2.35; 8.3.* lessThan 8.3.36; 8.4.* lessThan 8.4.27; 8.5.* lessThan 8.5.12; defaultStatus "unaffected".
- CVSS v4.0 9.2, AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N.
- Reserved 2026-10-12T21:03:58Z; published 2026-10-21T13:48:34Z.
- CISA ADP (Vulnrichment) SSVC 2026-10-21T14:34:39Z: Exploitation "none", Automatable "no", Technical Impact "total". ADP reference: https://www.wiz.io/blog/php2shell-php-rce.

# CVE-2026-109619 (cve.org record): notes
- Captured 08:12Z; raw/cveawg-api.json fetched 08:11Z.
- CNA PHP Group. Title "RCE via stale global state".
- Description (verbatim): "PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE)."

notes_md:
# Alexandre Daubois: "What the PHP2Shell rumors got wrong, from inside the PHP security team"

- URL https://daubois.dev/blog/cve-2026-109618-php2shell-rumors/ ; "BLOG · 21 OCT 2026", "REV 2026.10.21". Author joined the PHP Foundation in July 2026 to help the security team (per the Foundation's post). Personal blog, not an official statement.
- How the leak happened (verbatim): "An anonymous Hacker News post citing a reliable source went up on October 20 and came down, but screenshots of it had already reached X and Mastodon. A screenshot of the PHP2Shell tool, credited to Calif.IO, leaked alongside the advisory, and a short exploitation video went up and came down the same way. Then watchTowr, writing that 'we were all supposed to wait until Thursday at 11am ET', confirmed in public that the bugs were real and posted both CVE numbers."
- Says the CVSS 10.0 traces to "Florian Roth's post, as Phoenix Security relayed it" and to watchTowr via Cyber Daily.
- Facts box: "Advisory opened: 2026-08-27, credited to lcfr-hax, sagitzadik-wiz, amyb-oai and tomash-areion"; "Fix PR opened: 2026-09-25, final commit 01a40e89fbfc authored 2026-10-18"; "Leak and advance notice: 2026-10-20"; "Published: 2026-10-21, 14:00 UTC".
- Contradiction: the PHP Foundation says "No technical details leaked" with the CVE IDs, yet Daubois describes a leaked tool screenshot and advisory. Also "tomash-areion" is a fourth credited reporter not named elsewhere on this beat.

EADaily (Russia, Russian), 27 October, by Alan Pukhaev: 'PHP2Shell: how one hole in PHP scared half the world'. A broad explainer that mixes sourced and unsourced statements. It says the Netherlands switched off DigiD, the government portal, the parliament site, the Port of Rotterdam and some hospital and transport services as a precaution, Japan paused its tax service for hours and then Finance Ministry and big-company sites (Nomura, MUFG, ANA), and that the BreachForums and Dread forums closed on 21 October out of fear for their own servers (no source given). It says a story circulating that an autonomous AI agent breached a European ministry in two hours and that Lazarus was behind it has no confirmation in reliable sources and should be treated as a version, not a fact; and that a Polites News scan of 15 Kazakh state sites found two (ortcom.kz, bolashak.gov.kz) openly showing PHP 7.4.33. notes_md:
# Fastly’s Proactive Protection for PHP2Shell, Critical PHP RCE CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 | Fastly

Captured by claude-story-site. Status: captured. Candid on exploitability (PoCs need the binary's layout on x86_64; 32-bit assume compromise), on WAF limits, on signals (segfault bursts, workers spawning /bin/sh) and on more bailout paths to come.

- 'the existing PoCs require knowledge of the specific, running PHP binary and address space layout on the server for an attack to yield code execution on x86_64, so most deployments may be "safe" from RCE. Do not assume this holds true for you. If you operate a 32-bit PHP application, you should likely assume compromise.'
- 'The PHP source tree calls the zend_bailout mechanism many places'; 'Patching the specific paths that researchers demonstrated does not make the mechanism safe.'
- 'assume active mitigation will only serve as partial protection and may require blocking a substantial portion of legitimate traffic'.
- Signals: empty field names with deep nesting; PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS field; clusters of Apache segfaults then one slow 200; mod_php worker executing /bin/sh -c.
- Settings: max_input_nesting_level=4; session.upload_progress.enabled=0; pm.max_requests=50.
- Says PHP published patches for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 'for integration by package distributors'.

notes_md:
# PHP2Shell: Detection Opportunities · GitHub

Captured by claude-story-site. Status: captured. The most detailed detection guide found: verified ModSecurity tripwire on the upload-progress field, Sigma rules for the arm-phase fatal ('in Unknown on line 0'), FPM segfault correlation, Falco worker-exec rules, and the arm/fire success receipt in the access log.

- 'ModSecurity leaves REQUEST_BODY empty for multipart requests, so that rule never fires. Use the field-name rule.'
- 'a genuine memory-limit fatal cites the script ... in Unknown on line 0 means the bailout happened outside any script — the multipart parse.'
- 'reliable exploitation needs several attempts per target ... a burst of fatal-then-fire pairs is a tuned attacker. The SUCCESS receipt is visible in the ACCESS LOG: an arm-fatal burst followed by a fire that returns 2xx'.
- Reproduction ran on PHP 8.4.4's CLI server; nginx/FPM/Apache behaviour mapped, not observed.

notes_md:
# GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp (CVE-2026-109619): notes

- URL: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp. Title "RCE via stale global state". Published by bukka; page time element 2026-10-21T13:34:13Z. Captured 2026-10-22T08:09Z. GitHub API blocked for this session.

## Key facts (verbatim)
- Affected "< 8.2.35 / < 8.3.36 / < 8.4.27 / < 8.5.12"; patched 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, 8.5.12.
- "Critical 9.2 / 10", "CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N", "CVE-2026-109619". CWE-416/755/824/1325/1419 (same list as 109618).
- Credits: reporters sagitzadik-wiz, tomash-areion, lcfr-hax, amyb-oai; remediation developers arnaud-lb, iluuu1994, bukka, ndossche.
- Class: worker global state referring to freed request memory, "causing a use after free. A strategically crafted heap layout can produce full remote code execution (RCE)." Needs a producer and a consumer in different requests on the same worker.
- Confirmed cases: "PHP 8.5 fatal error backtrace: confirmed ... the basis of the confirmed mod_php exploitation"; "Session upload progress lifecycle: confirmed"; "Session lifecycle RCE was validated against mod_php and FPM."
- "Session upload progress is enabled by default, and no application call to session_start() is required."
- Mitigations: fatal_error_backtraces=0 (8.5), session.upload_progress.enabled=0, pm.max_requests=1; "Updating ... is the only reliable mitigation."
- "The confirmed impact is unauthenticated heap use-after-free, memory disclosure and remote code execution with the web worker's privileges."

# GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w (CVE-2026-109618): notes

- URL: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w. Title "RCE via OOM corruption". "Critical  bukka published". Page time element: 2026-10-21T13:34:25Z. Captured 2026-10-22T08:09Z.
- GitHub REST API (repos/php/php-src/security-advisories/..., /advisories/...) was refused for this session (repository not attached), so no JSON was saved.

## Key facts (verbatim)
- Affected versions: "< 8.2.35 / < 8.3.36 / < 8.4.27 / < 8.5.12". Patched: "8.2.35 8.3.36 8.4.27 8.5.12".
- Severity "Critical 9.2 / 10", "CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N". CVE ID "CVE-2026-109618".
- Weaknesses: CWE-416, CWE-755, CWE-824, CWE-1325, CWE-1419.
- Credits: reporters lcfr-hax, sagitzadik-wiz, tomash-areion, amyb-oai; remediation developers arnaud-lb, iluuu1994, bukka, ndossche.
- Class: "PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors ... leaves the request memory in an invalid state ... lead to remote code execution (RCE)."
- SAPIs: mod_php unconditionally runs request shutdown even when startup failed: "This happens entirely before any application-specific code begins execution." FPM: "susceptible, though no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated for this SAPI." FrankenPHP "likely susceptible"; LSAPI "application-specific exploits being likely but unvalidated".
- Fix: removes longjmp() for OOM; "delayed, graceful soft OOM" at next VM safe point plus hard OOM via _exit() at a higher threshold.
- "Complete remote code execution was validated over HTTP against mod_php with default PHP input and memory limits".

## Contradiction
- The Foundation blog says RCE "was also confirmed on PHP-FPM through application-level code paths"; this GHSA says "no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated for this SAPI". (Possibly the blog conflates with the 109619 session path validated on FPM.)
- The reporter handle "tomash-areion" is not named in the Foundation's thanks list.

notes_md:
# The fix commit, read from the repository

- Clone: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/php/php-src`, then tags php-8.5.11, php-8.5.12, php-8.4.26, php-8.4.27 and branches PHP-8.5, PHP-8.4 (depth 80) and PHP-7.4-CVE-2026-109618-109619 (depth 50).
- Fix: 3584a98bda0f2c0d367255b046798b0d3a221a19, "Avoid state corruption via bailout", author Arnaud Le Blanc, authored 2026-10-18T17:26:39+02:00, committed 2026-10-21T16:06:22+02:00, parent 512c04e39f. Co-authors Ilija Tovilo, Jakub Zelenka, Nora Dossche, Nicolas Grekas. Body: "Replace bailout on OOM with UnwindExit; Properly reset various globals that may be accessed during startup; Fix GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w; Fix GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp".
- 389 files, 10689 insertions, 976 deletions; 113 non-test files; Zend/ 96, ext/standard 52, tests 34, ext/mbstring 30, ext/gd 19, ext/date 17, ext/soap 14, main/ 7, ext/session 5, sapi/ 5.
- Merge path on PHP-8.5: Ilija Tovilo merges PHP-8.2 into PHP-8.3 at 2026-10-21T14:12:35Z, PHP-8.3 into PHP-8.4 at 14:27:03Z, PHP-8.4 into PHP-8.5 at 14:30:04Z; NEWS entry a34a205c2 authored 2026-10-18T15:34:31Z.
- 7.4 backport: 712e60f9edfd03f0960fc4fc3c2c375f42b90aa2, same title, authored 2026-10-18T18:09:54Z, "Minimal mitigation for EOL version", 17 files (Zend/zend_alloc.c +68, main/rfc1867.c +39, Zend/zend_types.h, Zend/zend_execute_API.c, Zend/zend_hash.c, Zend/zend_vm_def.h, main/php_variables.c, main/main.c, main/SAPI.c, ext/session/session.c, and headers).
- Mechanism (from the diff): zend_mm_check_limit replaces the bailout; a soft limit queues a delayed OOM (zend_mm_delayed_error) handled at the next VM safe point by zend_handle_delayed_oom via zend_throw_unwind_exit; a hard limit (memory_hard_limit_percent) ends the process with _exit; fallible allocations return NULL; globals reset in shutdown_executor, php_request_shutdown and sapi_deactivate; new ini max_multipart_body_parts; rfc1867 keeps only Content-Disposition and Content-Type headers and ignores duplicates.
- rjmendez's repository names the fix commit as 82f8f31b16a; not reconciled with 3584a98bd (possibly the PHP-8.2 commit before merge, or a cherry-pick).
- Not reached: 2024 history (shallow clone).

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

Hürriyet (Turkish): worldwide security hole in PHP; government sites were temporarily closed globally. # PHP2Shell: When PHP Runs Out of Memory at the Wrong Moment | Imperva

Captured by claude-story-site. Status: captured. Five demonstrated techniques, three via session upload progress; attack complexity high; ~67 KB memory disclosure; no matching traffic in pre-disclosure monitoring; '69% of websites whose server-side language is known'.

- 'Researchers from Wiz, OpenAI, and Calif jointly disclosed PHP2Shell'; involves 'session handling, OPcache class caching, and fatal-error backtrace generation'.
- 'Triggering the bug is much easier than turning it into code execution.' 'A later request must reach the same Apache worker and place carefully shaped data'.
- 'Three of the five demonstrated exploitation techniques use PHP's session upload-progress feature'; 'An attack can expose approximately 67 KB of process memory'.
- 'During this pre-disclosure monitoring period, Imperva observed no traffic matching the monitored PHP2Shell exploit patterns.'
- Settings: disable OPcache and upload progress as temporary measures; least privilege; IR checklist (child processes, file changes, outbound connections).

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

Kaldata (Bulgaria, Bulgarian), 26 October, by Emil Vasilev: the PHP flaws are now used in real attacks, with successful breaches. It relays BleepingComputer: Perplexity's Adel Karimi reported that his decoy servers recorded a successful attack on Apache mod_php with PHP 8.4.26, in which the attacker extracted about 800 KiB of process memory and then used an extracted function address in a following request, the server running the shell command about 1.6 milliseconds after the last byte; Expel's Marcus Hutchins confirmed the result. Cloudflare, Hadrian, watchTowr, Previdian and Patchstack had earlier reported attempts that had not led to successful exploitation, and Amazon had seen the first attempts on 17 October, four days before the fixes. It also describes the PHP security team's mitigation advice for a third flaw (CVE-2026-115560) that affects systems with an unusual configuration and has no patch yet: set session.upload_progress.enabled to 0 until it is fixed. A social-media post embedded in the page, an apparent tweet from a researcher about confirmed activity from the same IP and a second IP, is part of the article's embed.

> Компаниите Cloudflare, Hadrian, watchTowr, Previdian и Patchstack също съобщиха за опити за атаки, които към този момент не са довели до успешна експлоатация.

# ČVUT čelí kybernetickému útoku, údajně doplatilo na kritickou chybu v PHP - Lupa.cz

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`), page `cz/tech-press/lupa/cvut-cyber-attack`, snapshot `20261022T191510Z`. Copied byte for byte; every file's sha256 is in `captures/20261022T191510Z/provenance.json`. Publisher: Lupa.cz. Language: cs. URL: https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/cvut-celi-kybernetickemu-utoku-doplatilo-na-kritickou-chybu-v-php

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

Lupa.cz (Iva Brejlová) reports that Czech Technical University in Prague (ČVUT) is facing a cyber attack on its IT infrastructure. It quotes ČVUT's own statement from social media: the attack is "part of worldwide attempts to hit websites using PHP", the active attack was stopped, recovery is under way, and some systems were taken offline as a precaution. Lupa adds that ČVUT gave no more detail, that it is not yet clear whether the outage really relates to PHP2Shell, and that the international security community has so far found no evidence of real exploitation. An update at 19:30 added information on monitoring of possible PHP2Shell exploitation. The article also recaps NÚKIB's advice to update, the leak via Hacker News, and shutdowns in the Netherlands, Finland, France, Germany and of the Czech Government Office's website.

> „ČVUT v současnosti řeší kybernetický útok na svou IT infrastrukturu. Jedná se o součást celosvětových pokusů zasáhnout weby s technologií PHP. Aktivní útok se podařilo zastavit a probíhají práce na řešení a obnově. Do vyřešení byly preventivně odstaveny některé systémy,“ popisuje ČVUT.

_Curator's translation:_ "ČVUT is currently dealing with a cyber attack on its IT infrastructure. It is part of worldwide attempts to hit websites using PHP technology. The active attack was stopped and work on resolution and recovery is under way. Some systems have been taken offline as a precaution until it is resolved," ČVUT says.

> Není tak zatím jasné, zda nedostupnost jejích stránek opravdu s PHP2Shell souvisí. Mezinárodní bezpečnostní komunita, která situaci monitoruje, zatím nenašla důkazy o žádném reálném zneužití zranitelností.

_Curator's translation:_ So it is not yet clear whether the unavailability of its pages really relates to PHP2Shell. The international security community monitoring the situation has so far found no evidence of any real exploitation of the vulnerabilities.

## Why it is here

From the promotion queue (`index/promote.json`, priority 1): ČVUT says it faces an attack "part of worldwide attempts against PHP sites", active attack stopped; success unconfirmed

Copied byte for byte; every file's sha256 is in `captures/20261026T144241Z/provenance.json` and was re-checked against the watch's own hashes.

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

Digital Daily (Korean), 26 October, by Kim Bo-min: 'PHP emergency: now Node.js', a second runtime flaw a week later. It says Theori announced a Node.js vulnerability, 'Node2Shell' (CVE-2026-111497), a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that can cause denial of service, memory disclosure or remote code execution, fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1; this is a separate flaw from PHP2Shell, which TTMChange's report summarises (CVSS 9.2, mod_php the most exposed, code back to PHP 5.4). It gives a sequence of events: Amazon's honeypot saw an attempt on 17 October, details leaked on 20 October, Cloudflare applied emergency firewall rules and PHP published its advisory on 21 October, watchTowr and SOCRadar then reported exploit tools used in real environments, and on 24 October Palo Alto Networks warned its devices were affected. It also says the cyber-security firm Cyfirma found Korean-speaking members of a closed I2P network simulating attacks on the PHP flaws, aimed at government bodies, banks and other sectors in many countries, and raised the possibility of a link to the Lazarus group ecosystem with 'moderate' confidence.

> 사이버보안 기업 사이퍼마에 따르면, 익명성이 보장되는 폐쇄형 네트워크인 I2P 내부에서 한국어를 사용하는 특정 조직원들이 PHP 취약점을 악용한 사이버 공격을 모의한 것으로 나타났다.

notes_md:
# NCSC (UK) alert: Critical security issue affecting PHP

- URL: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/news/critical-security-issue-affecting-php (NEWS TYPE: Alert)
- Stated: "PUBLISHED 21 October 2026". JSON-LD `datePublished` 2026-10-21, `dateModified` 2026-10-22. HTTP `last-modified: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 07:30:02 GMT`. The NCSC all-feed RSS lists it as `Wed, 21 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000`, but every item in that feed is 12:00, so the time is a placeholder and only the date counts.
- Captured 2026-10-22T08:09Z (capture 20261022T080903Z).
- CVEs named: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Links to GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp and GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w (php/php-src), and to NCSC-NL's php2shell repo (https://github.com/NCSC-NL/php2shell).

## Exact advice (priority actions, verbatim)
1. "Identify systems running PHP across your infrastructure, prioritising internet-facing systems. As all versions may be affected, do not limit discovery to outdated PHP versions..."
2. "Update to the latest version of PHP and continue to monitor for future updates."
3. "If you are unable to update to a version with the security update applied, the PHP Foundation have provided temporary mitigations."
4. "If you are unable to apply the temporary mitigations, or applying them would take too long, you should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated."
5. "If you are unable to update or disable the system immediately then you should assess the system for any evidence of compromise ... and look for backdoors installed by an attacker."
6. Monitor third-party vendors that bundle PHP; points to the NCSC-NL inventory.

## Oddities
- The BBC live page quotes the NCSC as saying "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated." That sentence is NOT on the page as captured at 08:09Z. The page carries the offline advice as step 4 (quoted above). The page was modified on 22 Oct (last-modified 07:30:02 GMT), so the BBC may have quoted an earlier version, or a different NCSC note. Open question: find an earlier copy (Wayback?).
- "Organisations using any version of PHP are affected".

notes_md:
# NCSC-NL php2shell GitHub repository

- https://github.com/NCSC-NL/php2shell (EUPL-1.2). At the 08:09Z capture: 145 stars, 40 forks, 6 contributors.
- "Readme last significant change: 21 October 2026 17:25 CEST TLP:CLEAR"
- It says the CVEs are "tracked by CERT-EU as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619".
- Fixed releases: "PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35". Source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. Affected SAPIs: PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed, with the "risk highest for mod_php".
- Recommended actions (verbatim): "Identify PHP-based applications and their runtime versions..."; "Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, or apply vendor-provided backported packages."; "If immediate patching is not possible, follow PHP's temporary mitigations, including disabling session.upload_progress, restarting workers, and reviewing the official memory_limit, post_max_size and PHP 8.5 fatal_error_backtraces guidance. PHP states that these measures are not complete fixes."
- NCSC-NL does NOT advise taking systems offline, which sets it apart from the NCSC (UK) and the NSA.
- Links: CERT-EU SA 2026-018, ENISA CNW advisories/2026/CNW-2026-04_php.md, and php.net archive #2026-10-21-5.

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

Tencent News (Chinese), 21 October, by the creator account 荣姐聊AI (the page's disclaimer says creator content does not represent Tencent). A security practitioner describes what a traffic threat-detection appliance caught on the day the patch came out: several suspicious requests, one of which carried the User-Agent 'php2shell-scan/1.0'. The author is careful: the first requests looked like older, unrelated session-forgery attempts, a User-Agent can be set by anyone, there was no command-execution payload and no host-side evidence, so successful remote code execution cannot be inferred. The rest recaps the PHP advisory (versions 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, 8.5.12; Apache mod_php the most exposed) and the stopgap measures PHP published, which are not repeated here.

> 最后，流量中没有出现明显的命令执行载荷，也没有后端主机行为证据，因此无法据此判断攻击者已经实现远程代码执行。

_Curator's translation:_ "Finally, no obvious command-execution payload appeared in the traffic and there is no back-end host evidence, so it cannot be concluded that the attacker achieved remote code execution."

_The watch reader's summary (researcher@php.newsroom, of its snapshot 20261022T181608Z, not necessarily this one):_ Tencent News first-person write-up by a SOC analyst. On 22 Oct they used ThreatBook (Weibu) TDP traffic sensors to catch suspicious requests that abuse PHP's session upload-progress feature, including a scanner whose User-Agent was 'php2shell-scan/1.0'. They give a careful analysis of what is a scan versus a real exploit. A sidebar headline says MIIT issued a risk alert and Tencent Cloud and Alibaba Cloud published advisories.

_Curator's reading of the capture._

Notebookcheck (French edition, DeepL translation of Darryl Linington's article), 26 October: the fixes cover only PHP 8.2 to 8.5, leaving many internet-exposed hosts on versions that never got an official fix. A Shodan count published by Mallory on 20 October found about 884,000 exposed hosts declaring an unsupported PHP version, 59% of the roughly 1.5 million hosts that reveal a version, with about 740,000 more hiding it; CybelAngel's split is about 369,000 on PHP 5.x, 329,000 on 7.x and 186,000 on 8.0 and 8.1, against 612,000 on 8.2 to 8.5; Palo Alto Networks separately counted over 22.6 million potentially vulnerable instances. The article stresses these are banner counts, not confirmed vulnerable sites. It says PHP issued no numbered releases for end-of-life branches but minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, nothing for 5.6 or 7.3 and earlier; that distributions can ship the fix under an old version string; and that CISA advised taking PHP-based systems offline if they cannot be updated.

> Les correctifs de PHP2Shell ne couvrent que PHP 8.2 à 8.5, ce qui laisse une grande partie des hôtes PHP exposés à Internet sur des versions qui n’ont jamais bénéficié d’une publication officielle de correctifs.

> In Belgien war unter anderem die Website des Außenministeriums offline. In den Niederlanden waren der digitale Identitätsdienst DigiD, die Parlamentswebsite und der Internetauftritt des nationalen Cybersicherheitszentrums betroffen.

# CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`), page `us/security-vendor/palo-alto-networks/psirt-cve-2026-109618`, snapshot `20261022T191713Z`. ## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

Palo Alto Networks' security advisory on the impact of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on its products. PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2 are listed as vulnerable (CPE ranges). The issue strictly affects the PAN-OS management web interface (HTTPS web UI and XML API), and a dataplane interface only if a management profile is attached; GlobalProtect portal and gateway and the captive portal are not affected. Palo Alto rates it Severity HIGH, urgency MODERATE, with CVSS-B 8.7 when the management interface is reachable from the internet and 7.1 when access is restricted to a jump box. Both of Palo Alto's product vectors score availability impact only (VC:N/VI:N/VA:H), against the vendor (PHP) score it also shows, CVSS-B 9.2 with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact, while its own text describes the CVEs as remote code execution. Fixes will come in upcoming PAN-OS releases; until then: restrict management access to trusted internal IPs or a jump box, and Threat Prevention IDs 543004, 97622-97625 (content 9162+). Frontier Virtual Patching customers on PAN-OS 12.2.4+ received coverage via Threat ID 543004 at 10:21 PM PT on 20 October. "Palo Alto Networks is not aware of any malicious exploitation of this issue against our products."

notes_md:
# PHP Foundation blog: notes

- URL: https://thephp.foundation/blog/2026/10/21/todays-php-security-release-and-how-were-strengthening-php-security/
- "Published on Oct 21, 2026", by "The PHP Foundation". Captured 2026-10-22T08:09Z.
- The rendered page also embeds an r/PHP thread (third-party comments, e.g. a claim that the first in-the-wild exploit was at 08:36 UTC citing ellio.tech). That is not Foundation content.

## Key wording (verbatim)
- "CVE-2026-109618 / GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w: RCE via OOM corruption ... On Apache with mod_php, an unauthenticated request can trigger this before any application code runs, and full remote code execution was demonstrated with default settings. Remote code execution was also confirmed on PHP-FPM through application-level code paths."
- "CVE-2026-109619 / GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp: RCE via stale global state ... A use-after-free and worker crash were confirmed, and the reporter demonstrated remote code execution against a real-world application running on Apache with mod_php."
- 2024 audit: Sovereign Tech Agency funding, via OSTIF, carried out by Quarkslab; a Foundation-contracted core developer "found the first signs of the OOM problem behind CVE-2026-109618". "the delay was a structural failure".
- "security firm Calif began an audit of PHP on July 30th, 2026. On August 11th researcher Ryan A at Calif reported an unconditional remote code execution ... OpenAI independently reported the same root cause on the same day, followed by further attack vectors from OpenAI on September 18th and from Wiz on August 24th."
- Also mentions scanning with "Anthropic's Claude Mythos" via Alpha-Omega, and "OpenAI's Daybreak Red" for validation; Trail of Bits also auditing.
- "On Tuesday, October 20th, at around 15:00 UTC, the two CVE IDs began circulating on online forums and social media. They came with a wrong release time and a wrong CVSS score of 10.0 (the actual score is 9.2). No technical details leaked." Pre-announcement "published it at 19:30 UTC". Release moved "from October 22nd, 14:00 UTC, to October 21st, 14:00 UTC."
- "As a result of the leak and pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC, Calif ... mistakenly published a video."
- "Mitigation advice we started providing to a few critical infrastructure providers around Oct 20th 23:00 UTC, may have leaked as well." "did not identify any functional exploits at the time of release/public disclosure."
- "On October 21st at 07:41 UTC, more than six hours before the coordinated release, Chainguard unilaterally broke the embargo and published built images containing the fix."
- Thanks: "Calif, especially Ryan A, Wiz, OpenAI Codex Security, especially Amy Burnett, OSTIF, and Quarkslab".

## Contradictions
- BBC: Calif found it in August, OpenAI and Wiz "shortly after". Foundation: OpenAI reported the same root cause the same day (11 Aug); Wiz 24 Aug.
- Pre-announcement 19:30 UTC here vs php.net feed timestamp 20:32 UTC.
- The note's order of OpenAI 18 Sep then Wiz 24 Aug is as written (non-chronological).

# php.net security advisory: notes

- URL: https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-5 (news archive; the same page holds the four release posts and the 20 Oct pre-announcement)
- Captured 2026-10-22T08:09Z (capture.mjs); raw/feed.atom and raw/archive-2026.curl.html fetched with curl ~08:07-08:12Z.
- Publisher: the PHP Group / php.net. Date on the page: "21 Oct 2026".

## Key wording (verbatim)
- "PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately."
- "Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs."
- "RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w)"
- "RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp)"
- "PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project." Minimal source backports were published as branches PHP-7.4/8.0/8.1-CVE-2026-109618-109619 on php/php-src.
- remirepo: "The repo will not have updates today."
- Mitigations: memory_limit=-1, low post_max_size (8M / 32M), session.upload_progress.enabled=0, on 8.5 fatal_error_backtraces=0. "only an update is a complete solution".
- Pre-announcement (anchor 2026-10-20-1, "Upcoming Critical PHP Security Release"): "It is scheduled for Wednesday, 21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC." "It addresses two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2."

## Oddities
- Atom feed timestamps: advisory 2026-10-21T00:35:26+00:00; 8.2.35 00:05:37; 8.3.36 00:14:54; 8.4.27 00:20:54; 8.5.12 00:24:52; pre-announcement 2026-10-20T20:32:00+00:00. The Foundation blog says the pre-announcement went out at 19:30 UTC and the release at 14:00 UTC on 21 Oct, and GHSAs show 13:34Z. The php.net timestamps are the entry-creation times written by the authoring script, not verified publish times; do not use them as publication times without checking the php/web-php commit history.
- php.net's own date is 21 Oct; the BBC frames disclosure as 22 Oct (UK morning coverage). The original target date was 22 Oct 14:00 UTC (per Foundation blog).

notes_md:
# php.net PHP 8 ChangeLog: notes
- Captured 08:15Z (and curl copy in raw/).
- Each of "Version 8.5.12", "Version 8.4.27", "Version 8.3.36" and "Version 8.2.35" is dated "22 Oct 2026". The release actually shipped on 21 Oct (php.net news, GitHub release at 14:06Z). The ChangeLog keeps the originally planned date, and nobody has corrected it.
- Security line (verbatim, identical in all four): "Fixed GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w, GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp (Avoid state corruption via bailout)." CVE IDs are not printed on these lines, unlike earlier entries (e.g. 8.3.35 lists CVE-2026-91768).
- 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 contain only the security fix. 8.5.12 and 8.4.27 bundle normal bug fixes (GH-23644, GH-21999, GH-23980, a dl() use-after-free, etc.).
- The fix is "bailout": PHP's zend_bailout (longjmp) mechanism, consistent with the GHSA's description of removing longjmp() for OOM.

notes_md:
# PHP Foundation blog, 21 Oct 2026: the leak and the discovery timeline (collector-researchers)

Captured for the researchers/leak beat; the advisory collectors may hold their own copy.

## Discovery (verbatim)
- 2024: "While fixing one of the issues Quarkslab reported, a PHP core developer contracted by the PHP Foundation found the first signs of the OOM problem behind CVE-2026-109618. In 2024, a potential exploit for the OOM problem was theorized, but no concrete vectors were found".
- "The PHP Foundation got the PHP project into the Patch the Planet program, as part of which security firm Calif began an audit of PHP on July 30th, 2026. On August 11th researcher Ryan A at Calif reported an unconditional remote code execution with the same root cause as the OOM problem we had found in 2024. OpenAI independently reported the same root cause on the same day, followed by further attack vectors from OpenAI on September 18th and from Wiz on August 24th. More recently, Trail of Bits has also been auditing PHP."
- Tools: "Earlier this year, we worked with Alpha-Omega to scan PHP with Anthropic's Claude Mythos ... OpenAI's Daybreak Red for validating reports and exploits".
- Thanks "OpenAI Codex Security, especially Amy Burnett".

## Leak (verbatim, section "Leak and disrupted disclosure")
- "The coordinated disclosure of these vulnerabilities worked well until 2 days ahead of the targeted release date."
- "On Tuesday, October 20th, at around 15:00 UTC, the two CVE IDs began circulating on online forums and social media. They came with a wrong release time and a wrong CVSS score of 10.0 (the actual score is 9.2). No technical details leaked." Pre-announcement moved to 19:30 UTC; release moved from Oct 22 14:00 UTC to Oct 21 14:00 UTC.
- "As a result of the leak and pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC, Calif, one of the security firms that had reported the issues, mistakenly published a video. It showed their proof of concept working against a number of targets and revealed a few additional, though limited, details about the vulnerabilities. Copies of the deleted video started circulating on social media soon after. The video contributed to accelerated development of various PoCs".
- "Mitigation advice we started providing to a few critical infrastructure providers around Oct 20th 23:00 UTC, may have leaked as well."
- "did not identify any functional exploits at the time of release/public disclosure."
- "On October 21st at 07:41 UTC ... Chainguard unilaterally broke the embargo and published built images containing the fix."

## Odd / follow up
- Does not say WHO first leaked the CVE IDs, nor where. Daubois (same team) points to an anonymous Hacker News post.
- Text capture includes reader comments under the post (third-party; e.g. a commenter claims "sansec.io leaked one of the attack vectors ... in their page's metadata"; another notes ELLIO's first in-the-wild hit 55 min after Chainguard). Unverified.

# PHP2Shell: łatka PHP już jest, ale strony na WordPressie muszą czekać na hostingodawcę – Martin Cid Magazine PL

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`, read from its pack copy `7r83qic5`), page `pl/news/pl-martincid/technology-pl-php2shell-latka-php-juz-jest-ale-strony-na-wor`, snapshot `20261024T083755Z`. Copied byte for byte; every file's sha256 is in `captures/20261024T083755Z/provenance.json` and was re-checked against the watch's own hashes.

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

Martin Cid Magazine Polska (Polish), 21 October: why WordPress sites must wait for their host rather than update themselves. It says the flaws are in PHP itself, below the CMS, so a WordPress update changes nothing; PHP covers every web-request set-up (FPM, mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed), citing The Hacker News that an attack works even against a default 'Hello World' page, and that the worst case is mod_php. Wordfence says the patch cannot arrive through automatic updates, and Laravel Forge says Ubuntu's unattended upgrades do not cover PHP installed from outside packages. On package-source timing, mySites.guru reported that cPanel EasyApache 4 had fixed builds within minutes while Ondřej Surý's PPA and Remi's repository did not yet; only 0.08% of the active sites it monitors showed a fixed PHP at 13:52 UTC. It warns that backports by Ubuntu, Debian and Red Hat keep the old version number, so version checks mislead, and that long-running processes must be restarted. The fixed versions are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35; PHP 8.1 and older get no fix from the project beyond minimal source patches.

> Wśród aktywnych witryn monitorowanych przez mySites.guru o 13:52 UTC poprawioną wersję PHP zgłaszało 0,08%.

_Curator's translation:_ "Among the active sites monitored by mySites.guru at 13:52 UTC, 0.08% reported a patched PHP version."

# Vulnerabilities in PHP (PHP2Shell) Affecting Multiple QNAP Products - Security Advisory | QNAP

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`), page `tw/security-vendor/qnap/qsa-26-18`, snapshot `20261022T191720Z`. Copied byte for byte; every file's sha256 is in `captures/20261022T191720Z/provenance.json`. Publisher: QNAP. Language: en. URL: https://www.qnap.com/en/security-advisory/qsa-26-18

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

QNAP security advisory QSA-26-18, "Vulnerabilities in PHP (PHP2Shell) Affecting Multiple QNAP Products". Affected: QTS 6.1.0 and 5.2.11 and earlier, QuTS hero h6.1.0, h6.0.x and h5.2.11 and earlier, QuTScloud c5.2.9 and earlier, QuMagie 2.10.1 and earlier, Note Station 3 3.9.14 and earlier, QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7 and earlier, QVR Surveillance 3.0.3 and earlier (ARM32), TVR OS 1.0.4 and earlier. Both CVEs are CVSS v4.0 9.2 and can be triggered before application authentication; PHP fixed them on 21 October in 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12. "Exploitation attempts against PHP have been publicly reported. QNAP has not received reports of exploitation targeting QNAP products." Fixed QNAP versions are pending; until then: take the device off the internet (no port forwarding, UPnP, myQNAPcloud Link), use a VPN, restrict management ports, stop unneeded PHP-based apps, check for compromise. PHP in Container Station containers is not covered. The watch kept no page.html for this snapshot (rendered.html only).

## Why it is here

From the promotion queue (`index/promote.json`, priority 1): QNAP products affected; take NAS offline (primary)

Supports: cyber desk: appliances

# PHP-Lücke: BSI warnt vor Cyber-Gefahr – Firmen oft unwissend

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`), page `de/news/rtl/leben-digitales-php-luecke-bsi-warnt-vor-cyber-gefahr-firmen`, snapshot `20261022T181608Z`. Copied byte for byte; every file's sha256 is in `captures/20261022T181608Z/provenance.json`. Publisher: RTL.de. Language: de. URL: https://www.rtl.de/leben/digitales/php-luecke-bsi-warnt-vor-cyber-gefahr-firmen-oft-unwissend-id31448587.html

## What the page says

_The watch reader's English summary (researcher@php.newsroom, languages pass of 22 October 2026), not the publisher's words:_

RTL (dpa-based) reports the BSI has found no cases of exploitation so far and believes many operators have patched. Digital Minister Wildberger praised BSI and ITZBund and said shutting down sites was right; the Interior Ministry says federal sites taken offline are mostly back. Bitkom, eco, Green MP von Notz and the DStGB are quoted.

## Verbatim quotes, with the watch reader's translation

Each quote is in the snapshot as served. The English is the source watch reader's translation (`translations/de/news/rtl/leben-digitales-php-luecke-bsi-warnt-vor-cyber-gefahr-firmen.json`), not the publisher's and not checked word for word by the curator.

**agency**: The BSI said it had so far found no cases in which the vulnerabilities were exploited, though successful attacks cannot be ruled out.

> Das Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI) habe bislang keine Fälle festgestellt, in denen die Sicherheitslücken ausgenutzt wurde, erklärte die IT-Sicherheitsbehörde. „Dennoch können erfolgreiche Angriffe derzeit nicht ausgeschlossen werden.“

Daniel Scherzer's blog (English), 22 October: 'PHP2Shell: a Timeline'. The author is a PHP release manager (for 8.5) who says he was privy to internal discussions and lists only events and times verifiable from public information, mostly git history, GitHub logs and PHP Foundation posts, without judgement. Discovery: a 2024 security-audit tag in php-src (Quarkslab audit); a PHP developer in 2024 found the first signs of the out-of-memory problem; the PHP Foundation formed an Ecosystem Security Team on 18 May 2026; Calif began auditing PHP on 30 July under Patch the Planet, started finding code paths on 1 August, and on 11 August reported an unconditional remote code execution with the same cause as the 2024 finding, followed by reports from other organisations. Release: tags and tarballs for 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12 were made on Monday 19 October (07:30 to 17:19 UTC) but not published; the release was due Thursday 22 October 14:00 UTC; about 15:00 UTC on Tuesday 20 October online discussion of the CVE IDs, with some wrong details, led to it being moved to Wednesday 21 October, same time; a pre-announcement was posted at 19:25 and 19:33 UTC; about 20:00 Calif published a proof-of-concept video, later deleted but copied (a copy was online at 20:27). On 21 October Chainguard published patched PHP before release (07:41 UTC per the PHP Foundation; Hacker News reports say builds were available from 06:07); the fixes were published between 13:31 and 13:35 UTC, with source-only backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. Fixes had been shared under embargo with several vendors beforehand.

# PHP2Shell : derrière l’urgence des correctifs, les fragilités de la maintenance du Web

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`, read from its pack copy `7r83qic5`), page `fr/news/solutions-numeriques/php2shell-derriere-lurgence-des-correctifs-les-fragilites-de`, snapshot `20261026T170916Z`. Copied byte for byte; every file's sha256 is in `captures/20261026T170916Z/provenance.json` and was re-checked against the watch's own hashes.

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

Solutions Numériques (French), 26 October: behind the urgency of the PHP2Shell fixes, the fragility of web maintenance. Drawing on the PHP Foundation's account, it says that two years earlier, after a Quarkslab security audit, a developer working for the PHP Foundation had identified the first signs of the memory-handling problem later tied to CVE-2026-109618, that several fixes were studied but each had difficulties (possible incompatibilities, risk of new faults, changes needed across many extensions), that discussions dragged on in a team where only a few developers mastered the mechanisms involved, and that it took work by Calif and OpenAI in August 2026 to show that remote code execution was possible. _The watch reader's English summary (researcher@php.newsroom, languages pass of 22 October 2026), not the publisher's words:_

In a TEK Sapo opinion piece, Sérgio Silva of CyberS3c measures Portugal's PHP2Shell exposure. He finds 58% of 391 public-sector sites show PHP and many run long-unsupported versions, Shodan sees 2,339 Portuguese PHP servers (1,329 with no fix possible), the public school network is the biggest block, and twelve Évora district councils were patched within six hours. He also dates Portugal's CNCS alert to the night of 20 October.

## Verbatim quotes, with the watch reader's translation

Each quote is in the snapshot as served. The English is the source watch reader's translation (`translations/pt/news/tek-sapo/opiniao-artigos-exposicao-de-portugal-ao-php2shell-em-trinta.json`), not the publisher's and not checked word for word by the curator.

> A CyberS3c mediu nesse dia 391 sites do setor público: 58% mostram PHP, e dos 66 que dizem que versão usam, 29 correm versões sem suporte há seis anos em média.

_Watch reader's translation:_ CyberS3c measured 391 public-sector sites that day: 58% show PHP, and of the 66 that say which version they use, 29 run versions that have been unsupported for six years on average.

**number**: Shodan sees 2,339 Portuguese servers announcing PHP; 1,329 have no fix at all, only replacement, and the largest block is the public school network.

> No país inteiro, o motor de pesquisa Shodan vê 2 339 servidores portugueses a anunciar PHP; para 1 329 deles não existe correção nenhuma, só substituição. O maior bloco é a rede das escolas públicas.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Across the whole country, the Shodan search engine sees 2,339 Portuguese servers announcing PHP; for 1,329 of them there is no fix at all, only replacement. The largest block is the public schools network.

**patching**: Twelve municipal councils in the Évora district were patched six hours after the fix because they share a professionally managed platform.

> doze câmaras do distrito de Évora estavam corrigidas seis horas depois do patch, porque partilham uma plataforma gerida a sério.

_Watch reader's translation:_ twelve councils in the Évora district were patched six hours after the patch, because they share a properly managed platform.

**number**: W3Techs on 21 October: 74.4% of identifiable .pt sites run PHP and 66.1% of those with a CMS use WordPress; with about 490,000 active .pt domains, that suggests over 300,000 Portuguese PHP sites (an estimate).

> Entre os sites com domínio .pt cuja tecnologia é identificável, 74,4% correm em PHP e 66,1% dos que têm gestor de conteúdos usam WordPress, segundo o W3Techs, a 21 de outubro de 2026.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Among .pt domain sites whose technology is identifiable, 74.4% run on PHP and 66.1% of those with a content management system use WordPress, according to W3Techs, on 21 October 2026.

**agency**: Portugal's CNCS issued an alert on the night of 20 October, after the Hacker News leak.

> Nessa noite o CNCS português emitiu um alerta.

_Watch reader's translation:_ That night the Portuguese CNCS issued an alert.

**exploitation**: Cloudflare was already seeing first attacks at 07:43 on 21 October, before the patch.

> Às 07h43 desse dia a Cloudflare já via os primeiros ataques, antes do patch.
