# PHP knew about one of the flaws in 2024 but could not agree a fix

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`, read from its pack copy `7r83qic5`), page `au/news/thenextweb/wikipedia-ref-9-dation-structural-failure-2024-flaw-leak`, snapshot `20261025T114552Z`. Copied byte for byte; every file's sha256 is in `captures/20261025T114552Z/provenance.json` and was re-checked against the watch's own hashes.

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

The Next Web (English), 21 October: 'PHP knew about one of the flaws in 2024 but could not agree a fix', reporting a PHP Foundation blog post published on the day of the release. It says a core developer first spotted the memory-handling bug in 2024 while fixing a separate issue from PHP's first external security audit, that someone theorised a possible exploit but nobody found a concrete way in, and that the fix then stalled for months because the security team's competing repairs each carried a cost (one broke backward compatibility, one added a denial-of-service risk, one forced changes on thousands of third-party extensions). The Foundation wrote that the delay was a structural failure caused by the team's decision process and lack of resources. On the leak: on 20 October at about 15:00 UTC the two CVE identifiers began circulating on forums and social media with a wrong release time and a wrong severity score of 10.0 (the real figure is 9.2), with no technical details at that point; the Foundation brought the announcement forward and moved the release up a day, from 22 to 21 October; at about 20:00 UTC Calif mistakenly published a video of its proof of concept working against real targets, deleted but copied, which sped up public exploit code the next day; and more than six hours before the release Chainguard published built images containing the fix, which the Foundation says 'disregarded weeks of work by many parties toward a coordinated disclosure'. The team saw no working exploit by the time of release. The post also asks for money: the team published 15 CVEs since the start of July and worked through more than 100 others that proved invalid or duplicates.

> the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`), page `nl/news/tpo/tpo-nl-digid-offline`, snapshot `20261022T171501Z`. ## What the page says

_The watch reader's English summary (researcher@php.newsroom, languages pass of 22 October 2026), not the publisher's words:_

TPO reports that NotuBiz, used by about 100 municipalities, went down first, followed by the Dutch Data Protection Authority, the Union of Water Boards, UWV's sick-leave tool, RTL, ANP, the Schiphol app, hospitals and KWF; universities of applied sciences shut systems with SURF. It says all Flemish government sites and French prefecture sites went offline, and quotes NCSC deputy director Corine Schipper-Derkse and Justice Minister Van Weel.

## Verbatim quotes, with the watch reader's translation

Each quote is in the snapshot as served. The English is the source watch reader's translation (`translations/nl/news/tpo/tpo-nl-digid-offline.json`), not the publisher's and not checked word for word by the curator.

**offline**: Meeting platform NotuBiz, used by about a hundred municipalities, went down first in the morning, followed by the Dutch Data Protection Authority, the Union of Water Boards, UWV's sick-reporting tool, RTL, ANP and the Schiphol app.

> Vergaderplatform Notubiz, dat door zo’n honderd gemeenten wordt gebruikt, ging ’s ochtends als eerste plat. Daarna volgden onder meer de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, de Unie van Waterschappen, de ziekmeldtool van UWV, RTL, het ANP en de app van Schiphol.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Meeting platform Notubiz, used by around a hundred municipalities, went down first in the morning. It was followed by, among others, the Dutch Data Protection Authority, the Union of Water Boards, UWV's sick-reporting tool, RTL, ANP and the Schiphol app.

**offline**: The Netherlands Association of Universities of Applied Sciences said many educational institutions switched off systems and are working on recovery with SURF; charity KWF also went offline.

> De Vereniging Hogescholen meldt dat “veel onderwijsinstellingen” systemen hebben uitgezet en samen met SURF werken aan herstel.

_Watch reader's translation:_ The Netherlands Association of Universities of Applied Sciences reports that 'many educational institutions' have switched off systems and are working on recovery together with SURF.

**offline**: In Belgium all websites of the Flemish government went offline, and in France those of the prefectures.

> In België gingen alle websites van de Vlaamse overheid uit de lucht, in Frankrijk die van de prefecturen en ook in Finland grepen overheden in.

_Watch reader's translation:_ In Belgium all websites of the Flemish government went offline, in France those of the prefectures, and in Finland too governments intervened.

**official**: NCSC-NL deputy director Corine Schipper-Derkse stressed it is not an attack but a design flaw in the software.

> “Het is niet zozeer een aanval, maar een weeffout die in de software zit en dat kan gebeuren”, aldus adjunct-directeur Corine Schipper-Derkse.

_Watch reader's translation:_ 'It is not so much an attack, but a design flaw in the software, and that can happen,' said deputy director Corine Schipper-Derkse.

**official**: Dutch Justice and Security Minister Van Weel said there were 'no signals yet' that the flaws were being actively exploited.

> Minister Van Weel van Justitie en Veiligheid liet weten dat er “nog geen signalen” zijn dat de lekken actief worden misbruikt.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Minister Van Weel of Justice and Security said there were 'no signals yet' that the flaws are being actively exploited.

**agency**: NCSC-NL speaks of a 'very high risk of complete takeover of the system'.

> Het NCSC spreekt van een “zeer hoog risico op volledige overname van het systeem”.

_Watch reader's translation:_ The NCSC speaks of a 'very high risk of complete takeover of the system'.

Promoted by curator@php.newsroom from the source watch (vault `oq9gflln`), page `ch/news/watson/wirtschaft-schweiz-322033892-php2shell-laut-bund-keine-hacke`, snapshot `20261022T181608Z`. URL: https://www.watson.ch/wirtschaft/schweiz/322033892-php2shell-laut-bund-keine-hackerangriffe-in-der-schweiz-bekannt

## What the page says

_The watch reader's English summary (researcher@php.newsroom, languages pass of 22 October 2026), not the publisher's words:_

Watson (Keystone-SDA) reports the Swiss Federal Office for Cyber Security (BACS) knows of no attacks in Switzerland and has no reliable figures, but confirms PHP applications in the federal administration were affected. It names Basel-Stadt and Swiss universities as having gone offline, and cites dpa on German states, municipalities and hospitals going offline at the BSI's request, plus German MP Marc Henrichmann.

## Verbatim quotes, with the watch reader's translation

Each quote is in the snapshot as served. The English is the source watch reader's translation (`translations/ch/news/watson/wirtschaft-schweiz-322033892-php2shell-laut-bund-keine-hacke.json`), not the publisher's and not checked word for word by the curator.

**agency**: BACS said PHP-based applications in the Swiss federal administration were also affected and the responsible units were told to install updates quickly.

> Auch in der Bundesverwaltung seien PHP-basierte Anwendungen von den Schwachstellen betroffen gewesen. Die zuständigen Stellen seien informiert und zur raschen Installation der Sicherheitsupdates aufgefordert worden.

_Watch reader's translation:_ PHP-based applications in the federal administration were also affected by the vulnerabilities. The responsible units had been informed and asked to install the security updates quickly.

**agency**: BACS told Keystone-SDA it has no reliable figures on affected Swiss websites, shops or internal applications, and knows of no attacks in Switzerland so far.

> Belastbare Zahlen und Daten zu betroffenen Websites, Onlineshops oder internen Anwendungen liegen nicht vor, wie das Bundesamt für Cybersicherheit (BACS) am Donnerstag auf Anfrage der Nachrichtenagentur Keystone-SDA mitteilte.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Reliable figures and data on affected websites, online shops or internal applications are not available, the Federal Office for Cyber Security (BACS) told the news agency Keystone-SDA on Thursday.

**offline**: Websites in Switzerland shut down preventively on Wednesday include the cantonal sites of Basel-Stadt and online services of Swiss universities.

> so unter anderem die kantonalen Webseiten von Basel-Stadt sowie Online-Dienste von Schweizer Universitäten und Hochschulen.

_Watch reader's translation:_ including the cantonal websites of Basel-Stadt and online services of Swiss universities and colleges.

**offline**: Per dpa, several German federal states, municipalities, authorities, universities and hospitals took their websites temporarily offline at the BSI's request.

> Mehrere Bundesländer, Kommunen, Behörden, Universitäten und Spitäler hätten auf Aufforderung des deutschen Bundesamts für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik hin vorsorglich ihre Websites vorübergehend vom Netz genommen.

_Watch reader's translation:_ Several federal states, municipalities, authorities, universities and hospitals had, at the request of the German Federal Office for Information Security, temporarily taken their websites offline as a precaution.

**official**: Marc Henrichmann, chair of the German Bundestag's Parliamentary Control Panel for the intelligence services, called it one of the most serious security gaps of recent years.

> Der Vorsitzende des Parlamentarischen Kontrollgremiums für die deutsche Geheimdienste, Marc Henrichmann, sprach von der «ernstesten Sicherheitslücken der vergangenen Jahre».

_Watch reader's translation:_ The chair of the Parliamentary Control Panel for the German intelligence services, Marc Henrichmann, spoke of 'the most serious security gaps of recent years'.

# Wiz Research blog: "PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet"

- URL https://www.wiz.io/blog/php2shell-php-rce ; dated "October 21, 2026". Captured 2026-10-22T08:10:47Z, HTTP 200.
- 70% basis: body says PHP "powers 70% of all websites in the world" — a share-of-websites figure (no source cited for it on the page) that the headline turns into "70% of the Internet". Conclusion: "With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated."
- Severity claim: "These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history."
- AI: "We used Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol throughout this research. Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability..." Quote from Raluca Ada Popa, Head of Gemini Security, Google DeepMind. "a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work."
- Credits: "Wiz Research would like to thank the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI for their work on discovery, coordination and patch verification."
- Partners named: "Google Cloud, Cloudflare, AWS, Microsoft, Automattic, Fastly, Akamai, Imperva, Vercel and many others".

## Wiz's timeline (verbatim)
- "August 19, 2026: Wiz Research discovers the first PHP vulnerability using Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol."
- "August 20, 2026: Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against Drupal."
- "August 21, 2026: Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against WordPress."
- "August 24, 2026: Wiz Research reports the vulnerabilities to the PHP security team."
- "September 21, 2026: PHP acknowledges the reports and begins developing a coordinated fix."
- "October 21, 2026: Patched PHP releases become available." / "Public disclosure."

## Notes
- No mention of the leak, the Calif video or Chainguard.
- "September 21 ... begins developing a coordinated fix" conflicts with the PHP Foundation's account that fixing was "the top priority" "from August 11th onward" (Daubois: fix PR opened 2026-09-25).
- The BBC's "most severe ever found by AI" wording is not on this page as such; closest is "arguably in software history".

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

WWWhat's new (Spain, Spanish), 21 October, a webmaster-facing explainer of what the two flaws mean even for sites with WordPress, plugins and login up to date. It gives the fixed versions (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35), Wiz's statement that every release of the last decade from PHP 5.4 is affected by at least one, and describes the two classes of fault in general terms (failing requests that leave internal state half-prepared, and references to freed memory from an earlier request). It relays the PHP Foundation's timeline (the two identifiers circulating around 15:00 UTC on 20 October with a wrong publication time and a wrong score of 10; the release moved forward a day to 21 October at 14:00 UTC; one reporting firm published a proof-of-concept video by mistake), Cloudflare's WAF protections from 03:02 UTC on 21 October, DigiD and MijnOverheid taken offline as a precaution in the Netherlands (via NOS and The Hacker News) and BambooHR shutting its service in the US, Canada and Ireland, and Wiz's account of finding its first flaw on 19 August with its Wiz Atlas tool and the Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol models. It adds that PHP 8.1 and earlier get no project patches (minimal source patches exist for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1), PHP 8.2 loses support on 31 December 2026, and the Foundation has published 15 CVEs since 1 July. The author's own commentary is marked as his reading.

> Hay intentos de ataque documentados, pero ninguna intrusión confirmada públicamente a fecha de publicación.

_Curator's translation:_ "There are documented attempts at attack, but no publicly confirmed intrusion as of publication."

## What the page says

_Curator's reading of the capture._

Xataka (Spain, Spanish), 22 October: how to check that your site is safe from PHP2Shell. It repeats the emergency patch of 21 October for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, says Qualys states they can be exploited without logging in and Cloudflare reported attacks hours before the patch was published, and gives practical steps: find the PHP version in the hosting panel (cPanel, Plesk), run php -v on your own server, remember distributions patch without changing the version number so check the changelog for the two CVE numbers, ask the host whether the 21 October fix is applied, back up before changes, and watch for unknown files, new admin users and unexplained traffic. It says PHP 8.1 and earlier get no project updates, that Sansec said servers installing PHP from the Remi repository did not have the fix on 21 October, and that major hosts have patched all versions. It mentions a tool OpenAI published to check whether a site is affected. A header line credits Cloudflare with shielding the other 40% of the internet. Advice only; no new facts.

> Las distribuciones de Linux suelen parchear los agujeros de seguridad sin cambiar el número de versión.

_Curator's translation:_ "Linux distributions often patch security holes without changing the version number."

_The watch reader's summary (researcher@php.newsroom, of its snapshot 20261022T181608Z, not necessarily this one):_ Xataka gives a how-to for checking whether a site's PHP is patched (version numbers, php -v, hosting panels, distro backports). It cites Qualys, Cloudflare's report of pre-patch attacks, and Sansec's note that the Remi repository lagged on 21 October.
